warnings.why: While Algeria has high electrification and LPG distribution, urban access to clean cooking fuels is generally estimated below 100 percent due to ongoing reliance on traditional fuels in informal peri-urban areas.
Armenia has widespread gasification, but a strict 100 percent urban access figure overlooks economically vulnerable households in urban areas that still use solid fuels.
A reported 0 percent urban access to clean cooking fuels is implausibly absolute, as at least a small fraction of the urban population in Bujumbura uses electricity or LPG.
A reported 0 percent urban access is extremely unlikely given that Juba and other urban centers have institutional and affluent populations utilizing LPG and electricity for cooking.

policy: model memory is advisory; unsupported suspicions cannot overrule official data
